doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Chicago pianists, Tatum and talent versus practice
title: Jack DeJohnette and Herbie Hancock from Chicago
summary: Freeman says Jack played piano with him, and Herbie came from Evanston, not the clubs.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Cats like – all those cats who came out of here like – you had a lot of cats: Andrew Hill, Herbie Hancock, Jack DeJohnette. Did all those cats come up through your thing too?
Jack used to play piano with me. Herbie didn’t, but Jack did.
Where did Herbie come from? He came up in a different kind of way?
All right. Because people told me stories about him, and they always insinuated that he had a little money, or his family had a little money.
Maybe so, but he came out of a thing where he didn’t come up like the usual cats.
Not through the clubs and stuff like that.

Yeah, see, because they discovered him, and they made the hit Watermelon Man. He just – he started making movies, all kinds of different stuff. Of course he was with Miles Davis during Miles’s big years, when he had – what? – Shorter with him and Coleman, playing tenor.
